note:
"Plug DP" method (plug dynamic programming). The method extends to different scenarios, but the simplest starting point is to ask how many dominoes can be tiled into an $N \times M$ grid.

The idea is to setup a "fence" along one of the axies, e.g. the smallest, and push a notch from left to right, say, until it reaches the end. Across the fence is all a mask of all dominoes poking out from it. When the notch reaches the end, the whole thing is shifted.

```
 . . . . . .     . . . . . .
 . . . . . .  => . . . . . .  =>
 _ _ _ _ _|-     _ _ _ _ _ _|
 . . . . . .     . . . . . .

 . . . . . .     . . . . . .
 . . . . . .  => . . . . . .  =>
 _ _ _ _ _ _     . _ _ _ _ _
|. . . . . .     _|. . . . .
```

The mask is a binary value of whether the dominoes poke out over the fence, so scales as $2^M$, say, so only works for long "thin" rectangles.

To extend to multiple paths, an `id` is added, to tie the a path on one location of the fence to another. At each step, the ids are redone and reduced, so they'll never exceed $\lfloor M / 2 \rfloor$.

Transitions then become upkeep of the fence, allowed configurations from the current configuration and test for transition.
